points.text: Headline rests on bespoke GPT-4o metric without CIs, repeats, second judge or human study.
Judge prompt calls source image AI-generated though benchmarks contain real photos.
Independent CLIP metrics show near ties; VAREdit not best on CLIP-Out.
Comparison confounds VAR vs diffusion with data, base model and settings; no matched-data diffusion control.
Latency lacks hardware, batch, precision and step details.
VLM data filter discarding ~1M pairs not ablated.
First-layer sensitivity claim rests on one attention heatmap.
No ablation of SAR layer placement, alternative conditioning, or SAR at 8.4B.
Table 2 shows Finest >= Full and small SAR gain on PIE-Bench, likely within noise.
Eq. 7 ambiguous about first layer attending to finest source tokens.
Preservation claim contradicted by lower GPT-Over.; pixel-level preservation metrics missing.
Tokenizer round-trip reconstruction ceiling not reported.
Scaling claim confounds model size with training samples and tokenizer.
Optimizer, hardware, seeds, CFG/tau selection and baseline tuning unstated.
Minor: bold markup, Eq. 10-11 coverage, Size column, dataset naming.
Appendix numeric claims misstated ('215%', 'closes gap', 'vast majority of categories').
SAR evidence thin: one heatmap, single small ablation run, tiny PIE gain.
Evaluation depends on one self-defined LLM-judge metric without human validation.
Claims like 'naturally circumvents' diffusion challenges overstated.
No limitations section or failure cases.
Minor: dense Figure 2, Eq. 7 clarity, Size column, table grouping.
Novelty modest; related work omits controllable VAR/AR conditioning close to SAR.
Training-free VAR editor dismissed without numbers or comparison.
Claim AR offers better adherence and speed contradicted by EditAR results.
Peer-reviewed editors (MGIE, InstructDiffusion, SmartEdit) missing from baselines.
Standard benchmark metrics not reported; numbers not comparable to published tables.
Preservation story not borne out by GPT-Over.; gains from success score.
Single unvalidated GPT-4o metric; no CIs, human study or second judge.
Scale mismatch asserted from one example; Table 2 does not support it.
Data, base model and steps differ across methods; no matched diffusion control.
Data filter not ablated.
'215%' is a ratio; category gap claims overstated.
Scaling claim confounds size with samples seen and codebook.
Selection of eta and tau unstated while baselines use defaults.
Qualitative samples not stated to be randomly chosen.
Latency without hardware details; memory and token growth with resolution undiscussed.
Non-square and high-resolution images not addressed.
Assumptions that GPT judge and harmonic mean reflect user preference unvalidated; no user study.
Multi-turn and compound edits not evaluated.
Tokenizer reconstruction ceiling for untouched regions not reported.
No societal-impact or data licensing discussion.
No limitations section.
No evaluation on reasoning-based or multi-step editing (WISE, GEdit).
GPT-4o judge costly, proprietary, hard to reproduce; open-source judge needed.
Missing standard editing benchmarks ImgEdit and GEdit-Bench.
External VLM data filter non-reproducible; model quality may depend on it.
Related work and comparisons omit closely related editing models, including MLLM-based ones.
No evaluation of generalization to unseen edit types or few-shot adaptation.
No analysis of limitations and failure modes.
No user study; only CLIP and GPT metrics.
Only two academic datasets; no out-of-distribution or real-world evaluation.
SAR formulation underspecified (Down operator, masking, positional encoding).
Figure 2 omits components; heatmap colour scale unclear.
Filtered data details and release missing; code only after acceptance.
MLLM-based editors not compared.
SAR is a modest extension, not a substantial departure.
Attention heatmap analysis not repeated on tuned model.
GPT judges may be biased; human study needed to validate.
No comparison with frontier editors (GPT-4o-Image, FLUX.1 Kontext, Qwen-Image).
'First tuning-based VAR editor' claim false given NEP; VAR term misleading.

P.summary: Primary GPT-judge metric unvalidated; no CIs, second judge or human study.
Comparison confounded by data/base model; no matched diffusion control.
Scale-mismatch / first-layer claim rests on one heatmap.
Table 2 gains small and Finest >= Full.
Preservation claim unsupported; preservation metrics missing.
Scaling claim confounded by training samples.
Reproducibility and hyperparameter selection details missing.
Broad claims about circumventing diffusion overstated.
Modest novelty; related conditioning work omitted.
AR superiority claim contradicted by EditAR.
No societal impact or licensing discussion.

Q.summary: No reasoning or multi-step editing evaluation.
VLM data filter non-reproducible and under-described.
Related editing models, including MLLM-based, omitted.
No generalization to unseen tasks / few-shot.
No human study validating automatic metrics.
Heatmap analysis missing for tuned model.
'First' claim false given prior VAR-style editor.
